info.title: Touchline Match Centre API
info.description: Live, explainable commentary for synthetic football matches. Every club, player and event is generated by a simulator.

get.summary: What the service is, and where its data comes from.

post.summary: Starts an exhibition between two teams, with optional team sheets.

get.description: The demo matches and the stored ones, live first. If Cosmos DB can't be read, the list still answers 200 with the demo matches alone, and sets the Touchline-Degraded response header to "cosmos". The API doesn't enable CORS, so a cross-origin client sees the header only if CORS exposes it.

Touchline-Degraded.description: Present, as "cosmos", when Cosmos DB couldn't be read and the list holds the demo matches alone. The API doesn't enable CORS, so a cross-origin client sees the header only if CORS exposes it.

get.description: A fan match is Scheduled from its 202 until its first event is stored, 30 to 60 seconds later: it has its teams and line-ups but no events, and its stream stays open with heartbeats until play starts. A fan match that couldn't be started, or whose job never picked it up, answers 410 (type .../match-not-started) here and on its events, moments, momentum and stream.

get.summary: A page of a match's events.
Momentum so far, in five-minute windows.
Key and notable moments so far, with commentary for the viewer.
The live match, as server-sent events.
get.description: Server-sent events (text/event-stream). Each message has an event name, an id (the last event sequence the client has fully seen, for Last-Event-ID resume) and one JSON data line. The event names and their data schemas: state = LiveState, event = MatchEvent, moment = MomentView, commentary = CommentaryLine, analysis = MomentAnalysis, milestone = MilestoneView, momentum = MomentumReading, overlay = OverlayCard, shape = ShapeView (modelled player positions after an event, not tracking data), fulltime = LiveState (sent once), heartbeat = Heartbeat (no id). Without after or Last-Event-ID the stream starts from now, with a state snapshot. With after (or Last-Event-ID) it replays every message after that event, with only the latest shape; replay=true keeps every shape, for a paced replay (ADR-067). fromPeriod (FirstHalf or SecondHalf) and fromMinute, given together and without after, start the replay two events before the first event at or after that match time. The stream ends after fulltime.

schema.description: Server-sent event messages. See the operation description for each event's data schema.

post.summary: Ask the Analyst about a match.

requestBody.description: The viewer's favourite metric, such as `xG`.

get.summary: Archetypes, manager styles, crest parts and the squad rules.

post.summary: Checks names as a fan types them.

get.summary: The clubs, built in and fan-built.

post.summary: Creates a fan team, and returns its edit key once.

get.summary: A club in full, with its ETag.

put.summary: Replaces a fan team. Needs its edit key.

delete.summary: Deletes a fan team. Needs its edit key.

get.summary: A club's crest: generated SVG, or WebP artwork for the built-in clubs.

description.description: What the player is like, in a sentence.

ArchetypeOption.description: An archetype, as the builder offers it.

BodyPart.description: What a shot was struck with (ADR-019).

speedKmh.description:
The player's speed, in km/h. Comparing it with their recorded top speed (and spotting a
new personal best) is the milestones detector's job, not the event's.

CarryDetail.description:
The detail of a carry (ADR-019). The distance isn't stored: it's the gap between the
event's start and end.

kind.description: A possession, a moment, an event or the match summary.

label.description: A short label to show, such as `67:12 goal`.

Citation.description: Something an answer is based on, so a fan can check it.

CitationKind.description: What a citation in an answer points at.

minute.description: Whole minutes on the clock, counting on from 45 in the second half.

display.description: The reading as shown on screen, for example `67:12`.

ClockReading.description: A match clock reading, ready to show.

momentId.description: The moment it describes (string MomentIds.For(string matchId, long sequence)).

mode.description: The viewing mode it was written for.

CommentaryLine.description: One line of commentary about a moment.

CommentarySource.description: Where a line of commentary came from.

CrestEmblem.description: The emblem in a crest. The set avoids motifs closely tied to real clubs (ADR-031).

initials.description: One to three capital letters, or empty.

CrestSpec.description: How a crest is drawn: the service renders it as SVG, so no image is ever uploaded (ADR-031).

nextAfter.description: Pass this as `after` for the next page, or null when there are no more events yet.

citations.description: What it's based on. An answer with no citations should say it couldn't find support.

language.description: The BCP 47 tag of the language the answer is written in, such as `en` or `es-MX`.

FanAnswer.description: The Analyst's answer to a fan's question.

Heartbeat.description: Sent every few seconds when nothing else is, so idle proxies keep the stream open.

lastSequence.description: The last event included. Pass it as `after` to carry on from here.

fullTime.description: Whether the final whistle has gone.

halfTime.description: True from the first half's PeriodEnd until the second half's first event (ADR-066).

LiveState.description: The score, clock and totals at a point in a match.

ManagerStyle.description: How a manager wants the team to play. The style sets the team's tendencies (ADR-014).

description.description: How the team plays, in a sentence.

ManagerStyleOption.description: A manager style, as the builder offers it.

MatchAccepted.description: A fan match accepted and about to kick off.

dataSource.description: Where match data comes from. Always `synthetic`, because every club, player and event is generated.

fanMatches.description: Whether a fan can start a match now: the `FanMatches` flag is on and the launcher can start matches (ADR-072). When false the kick-off page shows Coming Soon.

MatchCentreStatus.description: What the Match Centre reports about itself.

startingEleven.description: Eleven player IDs, exactly one of them a goalkeeper.

substitutes.description: Up to int MatchdaySheetRules.MaxSubstitutes player IDs, none of them starting.

MatchdaySheet.description: The players a team names for one match (ADR-032): a starting eleven and its substitutes.

state.description: The score, clock and totals now.

homeSubstitutes.description:
The home bench (ADR-064), so a substitute who comes on can be named on the pitch. Empty for a
match stored before substitutions.

MatchDetail.description: A match in full: who, where, and the state now.

sequence.description: Position of this event in the match, starting at 1. Unique within a match.

matchId.description: The match this event belongs to.

possessionId.description: Which possession this event is part of, so whole moves can be grouped (ADR-008).

team.description: The team that performed the action.

playerId.description: The player who performed the action, or null for team events such as MatchEventType.PeriodEnd.

oneOf.description: Where the ball ended up, for passes, carries and shots.

successful.description:
Whether the action achieved its aim: a completed pass, a won tackle and so on. For a
shot it means on target, and void MatchEvent.EnsureValid() rejects a shot whose flag
disagrees with its ShotOutcome ShotDetail.Outcome.

underPressure.description:
True when an opponent was closing the player down (ADR-019). Only valid on passes,
carries and shots.

oneOf.description: Shot detail, present only when MatchEventType MatchEvent.Type is MatchEventType.Shot.
Pass detail, including xPass (ADR-019). Present only when MatchEventType MatchEvent.Type is MatchEventType.Pass.
Carry detail, the player's speed (ADR-019). Present only when MatchEventType MatchEvent.Type is MatchEventType.Carry.
The match's context (ADR-019). Present only when MatchEventType MatchEvent.Type is MatchEventType.MatchMetadata.
The card shown, present only when MatchEventType MatchEvent.Type is MatchEventType.Card.

recipientPlayerId.description: For a pass: the team-mate it was aimed at (ADR-017). Only valid on passes.

assistPlayerId.description: For a shot: the team-mate whose pass or delivery created it (ADR-017). Only valid on shots.

fouledPlayerId.description: For a foul: the opponent who was fouled (ADR-017). Only valid on fouls.

advantagePlayed.description:
For a foul: true when the referee played advantage and the fouled team kept the ball
(ADR-020). Any card follows at the next stoppage. Only valid on fouls.

foulSequence.description:
For a card: the sequence of the foul it punishes (ADR-020). Required on every card,
because a card shown after advantage can trail its foul by several events.

blockedByPlayerId.description: For a blocked shot: the defender who blocked it (ADR-022). Required on blocked shots, and only valid there.

oneOf.description:
For the ball going out of play: how play restarts (ADR-022). Present only when
MatchEventType MatchEvent.Type is MatchEventType.BallOutOfPlay.

replacementPlayerId.description:
For a substitution: the player who goes on in place of string? MatchEvent.PlayerId (ADR-064).
Required on substitutions, and only valid there.

MatchEvent.description:
One thing that happened in a match: the unit the simulator produces, Event Hubs
carries and the agents reason over (ADR-014). Events are immutable.

MatchEventType.description: What happened in a match event.

MatchKind.description: What kind of match this is, which decides whether it counts towards the season (ADR-020, ADR-021).

kind.description: Whether the match counts towards the season. Only a MatchKind.Fixture does.

season.description: The season, for example "2026-27", or null for an exhibition.

round.description: The round of the season, from 1, or null for an exhibition.

replayOf.description: For a replay, the match ID of the fixture it re-runs.

kickOffUtc.description: The scheduled kick-off time, in UTC.

seed.description: The simulator seed, which replays the identical match.

MatchMetadata.description:
The context of a match, carried by the first event of the stream (ADR-019), so every
consumer, including stream-only ones such as the overlay feed, starts with the teams,
line-ups and referee, and knows whether the match counts (ADR-020).

MatchPeriod.description: Which part of the match an event belongs to.

mode.description: The viewing mode it was written for.

source.description: Who wrote it: `Template` (built from the facts, no model call) or `Model` (the Producer).

oneOf.description: The home team sheet, or null for the engine's default eleven.
The away team sheet, or null for the engine's default eleven.

seed.description: A seed to replay a particular match, or null for a random one.

MatchRequest.description: A fan's request to play a match (ADR-032). Always an exhibition: it never counts towards a season.

MatchStatus.description: Where a match is in its life.

dataSource.description: Always `synthetic`: every club, player and event is generated.

crestUrl.description: Where the team's crest SVG is served, so a client never builds the route itself.

MatchTeam.description: One side of a match, as listed.

period.description: The half the event happened in.

MatchTime.description:
The match clock as a broadcaster shows it. The second half starts at 45:00, so added
time at the end of the first half can show a clock beyond 45:00 while still in
MatchPeriod.FirstHalf.

period.description: Which part of the match an event belongs to.

minute.description: Whole minutes on the clock, counting on from 45 in the second half.

display.description: The reading as shown on screen, for example `67:12`.

clock.description: A match clock reading, ready to show.

team.description:
Which of the two teams in a match. The home team attacks towards the far goal line
(X = 105) for the whole match. The simulator doesn't switch ends at half-time,
which keeps every coordinate comparable.

playerId.description: The player, if it's a personal milestone.

MilestoneView.description: A milestone: a first goal, a brace, a 50th pass, a personal-best speed.

kind.description: What a citation in an answer points at.

label.description: A short label to show, such as `67:12 goal`.

items.description: Something an answer is based on, so a fan can check it.

citations.description: The possessions and moments it's based on.

MomentAnalysis.description: The Analyst's explanation of a key moment, sent on the stream after its commentary.

MomentTier.description:
How much attention a moment gets. Key moments get the agents; notable moments get a
template line and no model call (backlog: the notable-moment tier).

period.description: The half the window is in.

fromMinute.description: The window's first minute on the match clock, inclusive (for example 45).

toMinute.description: The window's last minute, exclusive (for example 50).

value.description:
From -1 (only the away side threatened) through 0 (even, or no threat at all) to +1 (only the
home side threatened).

MomentumReading.description: How one window of a match tilted: which side was more dangerous (skill shot 2, match dynamics).

kind.description: What happened, as a key-moment or notable-moment kind name, such as `Goal`.

team.description: The side the moment is about: who scored, was awarded the corner or penalty, or was carded.

playerId.description: The main player on that side, if there is one.

reason.description: The detector's factual reason, such as `xG 0.41 from 11 m`.

oneOf.description: The commentary line for the viewer's mode and language, or null if none is written yet.

relatedPlayerId.description:
The other player in the moment, on the same side, if there is one: the player taken off for a
substitution (whose `PlayerId` is the one coming on), or the assister for a goal (ADR-068). Null for every other kind.

MomentView.description: A key or notable moment, with its commentary for the viewer.

NameCheckRequest.description: Names to check as a fan types them.

NameCheckResult.description: The verdicts on a set of names, in the order they were sent.

NameKind.description: What kind of name is being suggested or checked.

reason.description: Why not, in plain words; null when it's allowed.

NameVerdict.description: Whether a name may be used.

period.description: Which part of the match an event belongs to.

minute.description: Whole minutes on the clock, counting on from 45 in the second half.

display.description: The reading as shown on screen, for example `67:12`.

at.description: A match clock reading, ready to show.

type.description: The card type, such as `goal`, `card` or `milestone`.

durationMs.description: How long to show it, in milliseconds.

playerId.description: The player it's about, or null.

payload.description: What a broadcast overlay card shows.

priority.description:
How much the card matters (ADR-055): `high` for a key moment, `normal` for a notable
one and `low` for a minor one, which only the Analyst is sent. A client may use it to
stack or fade cards, or ignore it.

OverlayCard.description: A timecoded card for a graphical overlay on a live feed.

expectedCompletion.description:
xPass: the probability an average player completes this pass, from distance, pressure,
the target's third and whether it's a long ball. The passer's own quality changes the
result, not this number.

weakFoot.description: True when the passer used their weaker foot.

PassDetail.description: The detail of a pass (ADR-019, ADR-020).

matchId.description: The fixture it was taken in.

round.description: That fixture's round, so a history can be ordered.

sequence.description: The shot event's sequence, which orders penalties within a match.

keeperId.description:
The goalkeeper facing it: the other side's first-named starter, or null when that starter had
already been sent off, so whoever stood in goal isn't known.

oneOf.description: Where it crossed (or would have crossed) the goal line.

PenaltyRecord.description: One penalty kick, as both the taker's and the goalkeeper's record of it (ADR-021).

x.description: Metres along the length of the pitch.

y.description: Metres across the width of the pitch.

PitchPosition.description: A point on the pitch in metres. See PitchDimensions for the axes.

shirtNumber.description: From 1 to 99, unique in the squad.

archetype.description: The type of player, which sets the position and ratings.

id.description: The player's ID when updating an existing player, so their history follows them; leave it out for a new player.

PlayerDraft.description: A player in a team being created or updated.

PlayerPosition.description: A player's broad position, used to pick who performs each action.

season.description: The season, and the partition key.

teamId.description: The player's team, as of their latest fixture.

appearances.description: Fixtures played, starting or coming on from the bench (ADR-064).

rounds.description: The rounds the player played in, in order. The simulator reads these to know which rounds are done.

expectedGoals.description: The xG of every shot taken.

bannedRounds.description: The rounds the player is suspended for, in order.

recentPenaltiesTaken.description: The player's last five penalties, newest first.

recentPenaltiesFaced.description: The last five penalties the player faced in goal, newest first.

substituteAppearances.description: How many of the appearances were from the bench. A document stored before substitutions reads as 0.

PlayerSeason.description:
One player's season: the `player-seasons` document (ADR-025). It's rebuilt from all of
the player's PlayerMatch documents for the season, never incremented, so a
redelivered fixture can't count twice.

id.description: The player ID used in events.

oneOf.description: The player's archetype, for a fan-built team; null for a built-in one.

PlayerSummary.description: A player, as the UI shows one. Ratings and traits stay inside the simulator.

PositionMinimum.description: The fewest players a squad needs in one position.

PreferredFoot.description: The foot a player prefers to strike the ball with (ADR-019).

question.description: The question, up to int QuestionRequest.MaxLength characters.

QuestionRequest.description: A fan's question about a match.

id.description: The referee profile ID, for example `ref-pell`.

RefereeSheet.description: The referee named in the match metadata (ADR-020).

team.description:
Which of the two teams in a match. The home team attacks towards the far goal line
(X = 105) for the whole match. The simulator doesn't switch ends at half-time,
which keeps every coordinate comparable.

x.description: Metres along the length, from the home goal line.

y.description: Metres across the width, from the bottom touchline.

items.description: One player's modelled position (ADR-035), in metres on the pitch, to one decimal place.

positions.description: Every player still on the pitch, home team first.

ShapeView.description:
Where every player on the pitch is modelled to be after an event (ADR-035). The positions
come from a shape model, not tracking data, so they must never be presented as tracked.

clearedOffLine.description:
True when a defender stopped the shot on or near the goal line (ADR-022). It's still a
blocked shot, off target in data-feed terms, and the event names the defender.

goalMouth.description: Where the shot crossed (or would have crossed) the goal line, from the shooter's point of view. Null when blocked.

hitWoodwork.description:
True when the shot hit a post or the bar. On a goal it went in off the woodwork, and on a
miss it came back into play. Data feeds count woodwork-and-out as off target.

keeperDive.description: For a penalty, which way the goalkeeper went, from the taker's point of view.

expectedGoals.description:
The probability an average player scores this chance (xG), from 0 to 1. It includes
the body part, as public xG models do, but not the shooter's foot or finishing quality.

bodyPart.description: What the shot was struck with.

weakFoot.description: True when the shooter used their weaker foot.

situation.description: The kind of play it came from.

ShotSituation.description: The kind of play a shot came from. Shot quality depends on it (ADR-014).

minPlayers.description: The fewest players in a squad.

maxPlayers.description: The most players in a squad.

minimumByPosition.description: The fewest players in each position.

maxSubstitutes.description: The most substitutes on a matchday sheet.

maxNameLength.description: The longest name of any kind.

SquadRulesView.description: The rules a fan-built squad and a matchday sheet must meet.

TeamBuilderOptions.description: Everything the team builder offers: the choices and the rules.

TeamColours.description: Kit colours, as CSS colour values.

editKey.description:
The secret that allows updates and deletion, sent back as the `Touchline-Edit-Key`
header. It's shown only once and can't be recovered.

TeamCreated.description: A team just created, with the key to edit it.

oneOf.description: The manager, or null for a built-in team without one.

squad.description: Every player in the squad, by shirt number.

version.description: Increases with every update; sent as the `ETag`, and expected back in `If-Match`.

TeamDetail.description: A club in full: its manager, crest and squad.

shortName.description: Two to four capital letters for the scoreboard.

squad.description: The players: see the squad rules in TeamBuilderOptions.

TeamDraft.description: A fan-built team, as created or replaced.

startingEleven.description: The IDs of the players who start, goalkeeper first.

substitutes.description:
The IDs of the substitutes on the bench (ADR-064), in sheet order. Empty for a sheet with
no bench, and for a document stored before substitutions.

TeamSheet.description: One team's entry in the match metadata.

TeamSide.description:
Which of the two teams in a match. The home team attacks towards the far goal line
(X = 105) for the whole match. The simulator doesn't switch ends at half-time,
which keeps every coordinate comparable.

expectedGoals.description: Sum of the xG of every shot.

passAccuracy.description: Share of passes completed, from 0 to 1, or 0 before the first pass.

TeamStats.description: One team's running totals. Immutable: applying an event produces new totals.

id.description: The team ID, used everywhere else. Fan-built teams start with `fan-`.

shortName.description: A two-to-four letter name for the scoreboard.

origin.description: Built in, or built by a fan (ADR-031).

crestUrl.description: The crest as SVG, relative to the API's host.

ViewingMode.description: How a viewer wants the match explained (ADR-027).
